question: Does the times-through-the-order penalty justify pulling starters before the 3rd time?
answer: For an average starter, yes. The 3rd time through is +.022 wOBA over the 1st for the same pitcher, .339 against .323 for relievers.
findings: Within a pitcher-season, the 2nd time is +.013 wOBA over the 1st (CI +.011 to +.016) and the 3rd time is +.022 (CI +.020 to +.025).
Pitch count adds nothing: -.004 (CI -.012 to +.004) per 100 pitches, and the 3rd time stays at +.025.
The jump at batter 19 was +.017 (SE .003) in 2015-19 and +.000 (SE .003) in 2020-25, when it became a smooth rise.
Batter-adjusted wOBA: starters .321 the 1st time and .339 the 3rd time, relievers in inning 6+ .323 (n=664,061).
method: An OLS on PA wOBA with pitcher-season fixed effects, batter-season wOBA, platoon and home, with SE clustered by game. The starters who survive to the 3rd time are having better days, so if anything the penalty is understated.
data: Retrosheet play-by-play, 2015-2025 regular season, 1,109,963 starter PAs (1st-3rd time), 24,958 games. Retrosheet: the information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet (www.retrosheet.org).
split_check: The 3rd-time penalty was +.024 in 2015-19 and +.020 in 2020-25. The discrete jumps are only in 2015-19.
